title: The feature engineer and its feature language
request: Let a model propose features as small programs in a safe feature language (counts and shares per entity and place, ratios, distances, time since the previous row, rolling means) that code compiles into fold-safe features; on the fraud replica it should find the repeated drop-off and short-trip features without being told, and the ladder keep them only for a measured gain.
spec: A small feature language that code compiles into fold-safe transformers (15.4's behaviour recipe becomes programs in it); a role that proposes programs from the brief, the findings and domain knowledge; the feature ladder screens them. Done when on the fraud replica the engineer proposes the repeated-drop-off and short-trip features without being told, and the ladder keeps them for a measured gain; no proposal can read the target or the holdout.
plan: Write dclab_core/features.py: the operations (count, share, mean, deviation, ratio, value, since_previous, rolling_mean) over columns, distances, places, days and indicators; checks (no target, no forbidden column, an entity never a value); a compiler with an audit mode (up to the row's day) and an event mode (strictly earlier rows).
Write 15.4's behaviour recipe as programs in the language, and add an engineered recipe to the engine from project['feature_programs'].
Write the FEATURE_ENGINEER role (names and kinds only), its prompt, purpose and data-limit test; remove from the prompt the hints that named the answer.

Test with scripted programs: the two classic fraud programs lift the engineered recipe by more than 0.1 AP over raw columns on folds grouped by biker; no program reads the target; no test row changes a training feature.
Build the harness with engineer_gate_v1 fixed before any run; run the Step 3 reviewer; fix its findings.
Measure (ROL-002); fix the prompt for the failure it showed; measure again (ROL-004).
At the owner's request, write engineer_gate_v2 (measured gain on unseen seeds) and commit it before its first run; fix the crash the run found; run once (ROL-005); record v1 and v2 side by side.

decisions.decision: Features are programs in a small language, compiled by code, never code written by a model.
decisions.why: Code can check a program (no target, no forbidden column, no future row) and fit it inside the folds; free code could not be checked.

decisions.decision: The prompt does not hint at the answer: the line about 'the same place again and again, trips that end where they start' was removed before any run.
decisions.why: The package asks whether the engineer finds those features without being told.

decisions.decision: engineer_gate_v1 encoded the package's Done when: the two named shapes proposed, and the engineered recipe beating the raw columns by at least 0.05 training-CV AP.
decisions.why: It was the written definition of done, fixed before the first run.

decisions.decision: After v1 failed twice, the gate was not edited; v1 and its two results stay as recorded.
decisions.why: Changing a gate after seeing the result turns a measurement into a story.

decisions.decision: The second prompt teaches syntax with examples from an unrelated domain (customer orders).
decisions.why: It fixes the format failure without hinting at fraud features.

decisions.decision: engineer_gate_v2, a new version written at the owner's request after v1's second failure and committed (895b1e7) before its first run: on fraud replica seeds 1 and 2, never used for the engineer, with folds grouped by biker, the engineered recipe must beat the raw columns by at least 0.05 training-CV AP and match or beat 15.4's behaviour recipe, on both seeds.
decisions.why: It judges the measured gain rather than named shapes, on seeds the engineer was never run on, so it is a fresh measurement under a fresh gate, not a rescue of v1.

decisions.decision: An offline replay of ROL-004's programs on the v2 seeds, made while debugging the crash, showed seed 2 slightly below the behaviour recipe (0.551 against 0.562); the gate was left as committed and the live answer decided.
decisions.why: The gate was fixed before the run; what the replay suggested must not move it.

change: Step 3 of the plan built 18.4, 18.5 and 18.6 together and one reviewer read them together. For 18.5: dclab_core/features.py (the language, its checks, the compiler with audit and event modes, outputs named prog__..., 15.4's recipe as programs, FEATURE_ENGINEER); the engine's engineered recipe from project['feature_programs']; prompt feature_engineer.md pinned; the feature_engineer purpose and data-limit test; measure_engineer and later measure_engineer_v2 with GATES engineer and engineer_v2; tests/test_core_features.py and tests/test_roles_measure.py. Later: the prompt rewritten (11bab0d), gate v2 (895b1e7), the grouped holdout fold choice (12e7333).

findings.defect: Event mode was not 'strictly earlier' when timestamps tied.
findings.scenario: Dates without times, and a file sorted by label within each day: count by [entity, day] correlated 0.71 with the label, and a zero since_previous gap occurred in 100% of positives against 80% of negatives, because rows of one timestamp saw each other in file order. Rows with no time sorted last and saw every row; in audit mode the 'NaT' day string sorted after every date.
findings.cause: Windows used a stable argsort on time, so ties were ordered by file position.
findings.fix: The whole tie group is excluded from a row's window, and a row with no time has no history (NaN); the same window implementation was put into 15.4's behaviour features.

findings.defect: An exported notebook silently used the wrong recipe for an engineered project.
findings.scenario: A project whose ladder chose 'engineered' fell through to the raw preprocessing in the notebook export, so the notebook's scores would not match the records.
findings.cause: 'engineered' was neither handled nor in NOT_EXPORTED.
findings.fix: 'engineered' is in NOT_EXPORTED: the export refuses with a reason rather than writing a wrong notebook.

findings.defect: A program named like an existing column was silently lost.
findings.scenario: A program named biker_fare on the fraud replica collided in pd.concat; the engineered AP came out identical to raw, so the program had no effect and nothing said so.
findings.cause: Program outputs shared the table's column namespace.
findings.fix: Every program output is named prog__<name>.

findings.defect: The measurement credited the wrong programs as the gate's shapes, and the language accepted arguments an operation ignores.
findings.scenario: {op: count, by: [biker_id], of: {below: [distance, 50]}} was kept and counted as the short-trip share although count ignores 'of' (a plain per-biker count); any column paired with any place, the pick-up place too, counted as the repeated drop-off.
findings.cause: _is_short and _is_repeat matched loosely, and the language kept 'of' and 'per' on operations that never read them.
findings.fix: _is_short accepts only a mean of a short-distance indicator per biker; _is_repeat needs the entity and the drop-off pair; the language refuses 'of' and 'per' on count, share and since_previous, and 'per' on anything but ratio.

findings.defect: The ratio's floor was computed from each transformed frame and turned a tiny negative denominator positive.
findings.scenario: Fit rows and test rows got different floors, and a ratio's sign could flip near zero.
findings.cause: The floor was a statistic of the frame being transformed.
findings.fix: The floor is learned on the fit rows only (fit learns no label, only this floor) and the sign is kept.

findings.defect: In the first live run, 11 of the engineer's 12 programs were refused for carrying arguments their operation does not read.
findings.scenario: ROL-002: the engineer filled every argument on every program (for example a daily count per biker with 'of' and 'per'); the language refused them ('count reads no of or per: say what it counts with by'), including counts per drop-off and pick-up place.
findings.cause: The prompt's template listed every argument for every operation, while R4's fix had made the language refuse unused ones.
findings.fix: The prompt shows each operation with only its own arguments, with examples from an unrelated domain; re-pinned.
findings.test: ROL-004: all 12 programs kept, none refused.

findings.defect: The gate v2 run crashed twice, after its requests, on a grouped holdout with no positive case.
findings.scenario: On fraud replica seed 2, fraud sits on a few bikers, so the first stratified group fold's holdout held no fraud; the holdout AP was None and the final stage raised TypeError computing the CV-to-holdout gap. The two attempts sent 4 engineer requests, about EUR 0.003, and stored nothing.
findings.cause: prepare_bundle always took the first group fold, and the gap was computed without checking for a missing holdout score.
findings.fix: For a classification, the split takes the first group fold whose holdout and training rows both hold each class (decided before any model is fitted) and names that fold; a holdout metric that cannot be measured gives no gap instead of a crash. Reproduced offline with a scripted engineer before spending more.

measurements.name: ROL-002, feature engineer on the fraud replica, gate v1
measurements.gate: engineer_gate_v1: a repeated drop-off count and a short-trip share are proposed, and the engineered recipe beats the raw columns by >= 0.05 training-CV average precision.
measurements.result: 12 programs proposed, 11 refused for unused arguments; the one kept, fare per metre of the trip, lifted training-CV AP from 0.044 (raw) to 0.631, above 15.4's behaviour recipe at 0.452, on folds grouped by biker. Neither named shape was proposed. gpt-6-luna, 1 request.
measurements.next: Fix the prompt's template (each operation with only its own arguments) and measure again under the same gate.

measurements.name: ROL-004, feature engineer after the prompt fix, gate v1
measurements.gate: engineer_gate_v1: a repeated drop-off count and a short-trip share are proposed, and the engineered recipe beats the raw columns by >= 0.05 training-CV average precision.
measurements.result: All 12 programs kept (trip distance, fare per metre, rides per biker and day, per sender, per pick-up and drop-off cell and day, the biker's fare against his mean, time since his previous ride, a rolling fare). Engineered AP 0.589 against 0.044 raw and 0.452 for the behaviour recipe. Neither a repeated drop-off per biker nor a short-trip share was proposed (places were counted per day, not per biker). Owner's cap EUR 0.01.
measurements.next: v1 stays failed. The engineered recipe stays off by default. A gate that judges the measured gain would be a new version, fixed before a fresh measurement, if the owner wants it.

measurements.name: ROL-005, feature engineer on unseen seeds, gate v2
measurements.gate: engineer_gate_v2 (fixed 2026-10-12 before its first run, committed in 895b1e7): on fraud replica seeds 1 and 2 (unseen), with folds grouped by biker, the engineered recipe beats the raw columns by >= 0.05 training-CV average precision and matches or beats 15.4's behaviour recipe; both seeds.
measurements.result: Seed 1: 11 programs kept, none refused; engineered AP 0.607 against raw 0.056 (+0.551) and behaviour 0.502 (+0.105). Seed 2: 10 kept; 0.707 against 0.067 (+0.640) and 0.617 (+0.090). The ladder chose the engineered recipe on both. 2 requests, plus about EUR 0.003 for the two crashed attempts, within the owner's EUR 0.01 cap.
measurements.next: Record v2's pass beside v1's two fails. The notebook export still refuses the engineered recipe. The named shapes of the original Done when were never proposed.

outcome: Done under gate v2 (ROL-005: the engineered recipe beat the raw columns by +0.55 and +0.64 AP and the behaviour recipe by +0.10 and +0.09 on two unseen seeds; EUR 0.0011). Gate v1, the package's original Done when (the two named fraud shapes), failed twice (ROL-002, ROL-004) and stays recorded as failed; v2 is a separate, later gate written at the owner's request and fixed before its own run. The measurements also found a real engine bug (a grouped holdout with no positive) and a prompt template that made the model's programs unparseable. The review's tie-ordering leak was fixed here and in 15.4's behaviour features.
lessons: A gate that names specific features measures recall of an answer key, not usefulness; decide which one you mean before the run, and if you change your mind, write a new version and measure afresh.
Fixing one finding (refuse unused arguments) can break the next measurement through the prompt: re-read the prompt whenever the checker tightens.
'Strictly earlier' must handle ties and missing times, or a sorted file leaks its labels into time features.
Reproduce a crash offline with a scripted role before paying for another live run.
